title: MCP Server Security Checklist: 25 Controls for AI Agents
scope: Official MCP requirements and guidance are labeled separately from KyenAI operational recommendations. Validate each control against the named server, client, version, and deployment context.

controls.title: Validate access-token audience
controls.guidance: For HTTP transports, accept only access tokens explicitly issued for the MCP server and validate their audience before every protected request.
controls.verificationMethod: Send valid, wrong-audience, expired, and unsigned tokens to each protected endpoint.
controls.passCriteria: Only the valid audience-bound token is accepted; every other token is rejected without reaching a tool.

controls.title: Require per-client consent
controls.guidance: MCP proxy servers that reuse a third-party OAuth client must record consent per user and MCP client before forwarding authorization.
controls.verificationMethod: Authorize one client, then initiate the same flow from a new client ID while the original consent cookie remains present.
controls.passCriteria: The new client receives its own consent screen and cannot inherit the first client's approval.

controls.title: Validate redirect URIs, state, and CSRF
controls.guidance: Use exact redirect URI matching, single-use short-lived state values, CSRF protection, and secure consent cookies in OAuth flows.
controls.verificationMethod: Replay state values and try wildcard, changed, missing, and attacker-controlled redirect URIs.
controls.passCriteria: Every mismatch or replay is rejected and approved redirects use exact registered values.

controls.title: Reject token passthrough
controls.guidance: Do not accept an upstream token and forward it to another service without verifying that it was issued for the MCP server.
controls.verificationMethod: Present a token issued only for a downstream API and trace whether it can cross the MCP boundary.
controls.passCriteria: The MCP server rejects the token and never forwards it downstream.

controls.title: Minimize scopes and elevate incrementally
controls.guidance: Request the smallest initial scope set and add access only when a specific operation requires it.
controls.verificationMethod: Map every requested scope to one enabled method and run the workflow with optional scopes removed.
controls.passCriteria: No unused wildcard or admin scope remains and elevation is explicit and operation-specific.

controls.title: Protect and rotate secrets and tokens
controls.guidance: Keep credentials out of prompts, source control, tool output, screenshots, and ordinary logs; use managed storage and short-lived credentials where practical.
controls.verificationMethod: Scan configuration, prompts, logs, errors, screenshots, and source history, then rotate a test credential.
controls.passCriteria: No plaintext credential appears and the old credential stops working after rotation.

controls.title: Never use sessions as authentication
controls.guidance: Authorize every inbound request independently; a session identifier must not substitute for an access token or user identity.
controls.verificationMethod: Reuse a captured session ID without valid authorization and attempt calls against another server instance.
controls.passCriteria: The request is rejected and the session ID alone grants no capability.

controls.title: Secure, bind, rotate, and expire session IDs
controls.guidance: Generate non-deterministic session IDs, bind them to authorized user context, and rotate or expire them to limit hijacking.
controls.verificationMethod: Test predictable IDs, cross-user reuse, cross-instance replay, and expired-session behavior.
controls.passCriteria: IDs are unguessable, user-bound, time-bounded, and rejected outside their authorized context.

controls.title: Allow only safe authorization URL schemes
controls.guidance: Accept HTTPS authorization URLs in production and reject javascript:, data:, file:, vbscript:, and other executable schemes.
controls.verificationMethod: Return authorization endpoints using unsafe schemes, encoded variants, and HTTP on non-loopback hosts.
controls.passCriteria: Only HTTPS production URLs and explicitly allowed loopback development URLs open.

controls.title: Open authorization URLs without a shell
controls.guidance: Use platform URL APIs rather than cmd, sh, PowerShell, or interpolated shell commands when opening authorization links.
controls.verificationMethod: Supply URLs containing shell metacharacters, quotes, spaces, and encoded command separators.
controls.passCriteria: The URL is parsed as data, no shell starts, and suspicious values are rejected and logged.

controls.title: Block SSRF to private and metadata ranges
controls.guidance: Validate OAuth discovery URLs and block loopback, private, link-local, reserved, and cloud metadata destinations outside explicit development exceptions.
controls.verificationMethod: Try IPv4, IPv6, encoded, hostname, and cloud-metadata targets through every URL-fetching path.
controls.passCriteria: All private or reserved destinations are blocked before connection and responses are not reflected.

controls.title: Revalidate redirects and DNS results
controls.guidance: Apply URL and IP validation to every redirect hop and defend against DNS rebinding or time-of-check/time-of-use changes.
controls.verificationMethod: Use redirect chains and a test hostname that changes from a public to a private address.
controls.passCriteria: Every hop is revalidated and a destination change to a blocked address terminates the request.

controls.title: Enforce an outbound network allowlist
controls.guidance: Route server-side discovery and tool traffic through network policy or an egress proxy that permits only declared destinations.
controls.verificationMethod: Attempt direct IP, undeclared domain, private range, redirect, and DNS-rebinding egress from the runtime.
controls.passCriteria: Only reviewed destinations succeed and bypass paths cannot reach undeclared networks.

controls.title: Require consent before local server installation
controls.guidance: Before one-click local setup, show the exact command and explain that it executes with the client's local privileges.
controls.verificationMethod: Start installation from a deep link or imported configuration and inspect the complete pre-execution consent flow.
controls.passCriteria: No command runs before explicit approval and the user can cancel without side effects.

controls.title: Display full commands and dangerous-pattern warnings
controls.guidance: Do not truncate local startup commands; highlight sudo, destructive deletion, network calls, and access to sensitive paths.
controls.verificationMethod: Test long, multiline, obfuscated, and destructive commands in the installation dialog.
controls.passCriteria: The entire command is visible and dangerous patterns produce a clear warning before approval.

controls.title: Sandbox local MCP servers
controls.guidance: Run local servers with minimal filesystem, process, and network privileges and require explicit grants for additional access.
controls.verificationMethod: Attempt to read outside allowed roots, spawn child processes, reach the network, and access system credentials.
controls.passCriteria: Default-denied actions fail and each additional privilege requires a narrow explicit grant.

controls.title: Restrict stdio proxy process spawning
controls.guidance: When a proxy can spawn stdio servers, isolate the proxy, authorize dangerous commands separately, and log process creation.
controls.verificationMethod: Use a compromised-client test to request an arbitrary executable, unexpected arguments, and access outside the sandbox.
controls.passCriteria: Unapproved commands and arguments are denied and allowed process creation is attributable and contained.

controls.title: Inventory and scope every exposed tool
controls.guidance: Decide visibility, callability, target scope, owner, rollback path, and approval policy for each tool rather than trusting one server-wide grant.
controls.verificationMethod: Enumerate tools with MCP Inspector and compare them with the approved capability inventory.
controls.passCriteria: Every exposed tool has a declared workflow and no undeclared or wildcard capability remains.

controls.title: Separate read, write, and delete capabilities
controls.guidance: Offer a useful read-only profile without bundling mutation, deletion, secret, network, or production permissions.
controls.verificationMethod: Run the read-only workflow and attempt every mutation and deletion method with the same identity.
controls.passCriteria: Reads work within declared roots while all write and delete attempts are denied.

controls.title: Contain prompt-injection-triggered tool calls
controls.guidance: Treat repository text, webpages, issues, and tool output as untrusted data that cannot widen tool permissions or bypass approval gates.
controls.verificationMethod: Place malicious instructions in each untrusted input source and observe requested tool calls and permission changes.
controls.passCriteria: Untrusted content cannot expand authority, reveal credentials, or execute a consequential call without policy approval.

controls.title: Require human approval for consequential actions
controls.guidance: Pause immediately before destructive writes, secret use, production access, irreversible external messages, or permission expansion.
controls.verificationMethod: Simulate each consequential action and inspect the approval prompt, actor, target, rollback limits, and timeout behavior.
controls.passCriteria: The action cannot proceed without an informed, current, target-specific approval.

controls.title: Keep attributable, secret-redacted audit logs
controls.guidance: Record actor, session, server version, method, target, approval, timestamp, and outcome while excluding tokens and unnecessary payloads.
controls.verificationMethod: Run allowed and denied calls, then reconstruct them from logs and scan the records for credential patterns.
controls.passCriteria: A reviewer can reconstruct consequential calls and no secret or sensitive payload is exposed.

controls.title: Pin and review server supply-chain inputs
controls.guidance: Use trusted distribution sources, pin reviewed versions or integrity records, inventory dependencies, and avoid unattended latest-version execution.
controls.verificationMethod: Rebuild from a clean environment and compare resolved packages, checksums, publisher identity, and startup command with the review record.
controls.passCriteria: The reviewed artifact is reproducible and an unexpected publisher, version, or dependency blocks launch.

controls.title: Test revocation and incident response
controls.guidance: Maintain a fast path to disable the server, revoke credentials and client access, preserve relevant records, and assess affected systems.
controls.verificationMethod: Run a tabletop incident, disable the server, revoke a test credential, and attempt the former workflow again.
controls.passCriteria: Old access fails immediately, owners receive evidence, and restoration requires a documented decision.

controls.title: Validate allow and deny paths with MCP Inspector
controls.guidance: Enumerate resources, prompts, tools, notifications, and protocol exchanges, then test both expected success and expected failure behavior.
controls.verificationMethod: Run the Inspector against the exact reviewed server version and preserve results for every enabled capability.
controls.passCriteria: The exposed surface matches inventory, allow cases work, deny cases stay denied, and errors reveal no secrets.
